m:oldtown: The square can always be seen for free. The House of the Blackheads is open every day from 10am to 5pm (official website melngalvjunams.lv), but it closes on event days: the website listed closures on 14, 15 and 16 October and reduced hours (10am–2pm) on 28 October, without saying which year, so to be confirmed. Ticket €10; with coffee €12; reduced €6 for students and seniors; audio guide €4.
m:peter: A single ticket for church and tower: €9 (€7 for students), free under 7 (from a guide, not from the church website: to be confirmed on peterbaznica.riga.lv). Closed on Mondays. Exact hours change with the season: it usually opens mid-morning and closes in the late afternoon, but I couldn't find the updated winter hours. When the sky is overcast the tower loses its appeal.
m:dom: Open Monday to Saturday from 10am to 5pm and Sunday from 2pm to 5pm (doms.lv website). Entry €5 for adults, €3 for ages 11 to 18, free under 10. Hours change through the week: the website has a file with the timetable for 9–19 October 2026, check it beforehand. The church often hosts organ concerts.
m:tre: They're all outside and free to see, at any hour. If you have time, step into the courtyards: they're often open and free of tourists.
m:freedom: The monument can always be seen, for free. In front there's a very simple changing of the honour guard: I haven't checked the times. The park is freely accessible; from December to January it's lit up.
m:market: Entry is free. The market is open every day: the outdoor areas from 7am to 6pm and the pavilions usually from 7:30am to 5–6pm (centraltirgus.lv; individual stalls close earlier, especially on weekdays). In the evening from 5:30pm there's a farmers' market (times to be confirmed). Small stalls often take cash only.
m:artn: Free to walk. Almost all the buildings are private homes: you see them from outside. To see the interiors there's the Art Nouveau museum (next stop). Alberta iela is 15–20 minutes' walk from the Old Town, or a short tram or taxi ride.
m:artnm: Open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm, closed on Mondays (from a guide, not from the jugendstils.riga.lv website: to be confirmed). Ticket about €9 for adults, €5 for students and seniors. Hours change on national holidays.
m:occ: Open every day from 10am to 6pm, closed on 1 January, 23–24 June and 24, 25, 26 and 31 December (okupacijasmuzejs.lv website). Entry €8, students €5, audio guide €4; guided tours at 11am, noon, 1, 2, 3 and 4pm. Free on 18 November. The website said «closed» when I read it: check the day's hours.
m:lnma: Open Tuesday to Thursday from 10am to 6pm, Friday until 8pm, Saturday and Sunday 10am–5pm; closed on Mondays and some holidays, such as 24–26 and 31 December (from a guide: to be confirmed on lnmm.gov.lv). The combined ticket costs about €15, the permanent collection alone less (the figures I found don't agree: check the website). On the last Sunday of the month entry is free.
vd:milda: A Latvian restaurant right in the old town with simple, well-made cooking: pelēkie zirņi, grey peas with bacon and sour cream, considered the national dish, but also pelmeni and meat dishes.
vp:milda: Mid-range (€€): a main course is around €10–16 (menu not seen). Closed on Mondays. Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:pet: A tavern in the old town open since 1978, with traditional Latvian cooking: grey peas with bacon, roast pork and karbonāde, the breaded cutlet with sides.
vp:pet: Mid-range (€€): a dish is around €10–15 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:domini: More modern Latvian cooking, with farm vegetables, wild mushrooms and forest berries: in autumn there's the seasonal mushroom dish. A little more refined than the places nearby.
vp:domini: Mid-range (€€): a main course is around €14–20 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:ala: An underground cellar in the Old Town, a haunt for Latvian folk music, with 32 local beers on tap. Good simple dishes like grey peas and pork knuckle.
vp:ala: Mid-range (€€): a dish is around €10–15, a beer around €4–6 (menu not seen). There's often live music in the evening. Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:rozen: A medieval-themed restaurant under Cathedral Square, in a candlelit cellar: dishes like stewed rabbit, roast duck or lamb, and honey beer. Best to book.
vp:rozen: Mid-range (€€–€€€): a main course is around €15–25 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed. Position on the map is approximate.
vd:miit: A small roastery with specialty coffee and an all-vegetarian menu: breakfasts, light lunches and cakes. A good place to start the day or take a break, a few minutes from Alberta iela.
vp:miit: Budget (€): breakfast and coffee around €6–10 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:rocket: A Riga coffee shop, part of a small chain of local cafés with their own roastery: excellent flat white and filter, a few pastries and sandwiches. It has several locations in the city; this one is in the centre.
vp:rocket: Budget (€): a coffee with a pastry is around €5–9 (menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
vd:innocent: A neighbourhood brunch café: eggs Benedict on Latvian rye bread, flat white and macchiato. It fills up at weekends; better to go on a weekday.
vp:innocent: Budget to mid (€): a brunch is around €8–14 (menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed. Position on the map is approximate.
vd:mercato: Inside the central market pavilions there are stalls where you eat pīrāgi (bacon and onion pastries), soups and rye bread, standing or at little tables. It's the cheapest and most Latvian lunch possible.
vp:mercato: Very cheap (€): a pīrāgs costs around €1, a soup €3–5 (estimated prices, not read). Market hours from centraltirgus.lv; the stalls close earlier. Often cash only.
cd:cornerhouse: The guided tour of the Latvian KGB headquarters, with the cells and offices.
cn:navigazione: Museum of the History of Riga and Navigation
cd:navigazione: A collection on the city's history, next to the cathedral.
cd:etnografico: Wooden farmhouses, churches and mills from every Latvian region, on a lake.
cx:etnografico: It's about 10 km from the centre.
cd:zooriga: A zoo in the Mežaparks woods, a few kilometres from the centre.
cd:canalriga: An hour on the canal and the Daugava river, below the city walls.
cd:laima: The story of Latvian chocolate, with tastings and workshops.
cd:ebraico: The history of Latvia's Jewish community and the Holocaust.
cd:torretv: Europe's third-tallest tower, with an observation deck at 97 metres.
